muted-foreground.note: Darkened from shadcn's stock oklch(0.556), which measured 4.35:1 on muted and missed WCAG 1.4.3's 4.5:1 for body text. Measures 4.82:1 on muted, 5.25:1 on background.

muted.note: Serves as muted, secondary and accent at once. The system's only tonal fill.

border.note: Translucent white in dark mode, so it reads as an edge catching light rather than a drawn line.

ring.note: Darkened from shadcn's stock oklch(0.708), which measured 2.59:1 on background and missed WCAG 1.4.11. Measures 7.44:1 light, 4.67:1 on dark muted. Recomputed by meta.test.ts.

destructive.note: Used as text over a 10% tint, never as a solid fill. Solid measures 4.76:1 light, 6.19:1 dark.

priority-urgent.note: The only priority with a colour of its own; medium and high escalate by glyph and weight instead.

title.purpose: Dialog, sheet and alert titles only. The largest type in the product, used at most twice per screen.

body.purpose: The working size, and by a wide margin the most common (52 of 93 type utilities): row titles, popover sentences, form values, menu items.

label.purpose: Buttons, column headings, nav items, field labels. Same size as body, separated only by weight.

caption.purpose: Metadata, counts, timestamps, empty-state hints, badge text.

shadows.name: floating-layer
shadows.purpose: Popovers and dropdown menus: shadow-md paired with ring-1. The ring defines the edge; the shadow only separates from what is beneath.

shadows.name: overlay-panel
shadows.purpose: Sheets and sub-menus, which cover more of the page and need more separation.

shadows.name: ghost-border
shadows.purpose: Dialogs. A ring where a shadow would conventionally go, so the dialog reads as a plate laid on the surface rather than hovering over it, and the overlay does not muddy in dark mode.

shadows.name: avatar-separator
shadows.purpose: Peer avatars only, so overlapping discs read as separate people. Not elevation.

motion.name: duration-ui
motion.purpose: Default for dialogs, popovers, dropdowns and colour transitions. The ceiling for interface motion.

motion.name: duration-panel
motion.purpose: Sheet slide-in, the one surface large enough to justify longer.

motion.name: duration-flip
motion.purpose: FLIP_DURATION_MS: board card reordering via animate:flip. Set to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion, because WAAPI timings ignore the CSS reduce block entirely.

motion.name: touch-drag-delay
motion.purpose: TOUCH_DRAG_DELAY_MS: long-press before a touch drag begins, so a tap to open a card is never read as a drag.

motion.name: duration-trace
motion.purpose: TRACE_MS: the remote-change trace on a row or card, opacity only (8% rise, hold to 40%, long ease out). The sanctioned exception to the 100-200ms budget: it is news about something the viewer did not do, not feedback on something they did. A continued run starts at full strength (TRACE_HOLD_FROM_MS) so a peer's typing never blinks it. Under prefers-reduced-motion its own block sets animation: none, so it shows as a state for 1.2s rather than being cut to an invisible 0.01ms.

motion.name: duration-notice
motion.purpose: The off-screen remote notice's fade-in, replayed for news only; a peer still typing on the same issue rewrites the sentence in place. Shown for 4s.

motion.name: reduce
motion.purpose: Every animation and transition under prefers-reduced-motion, via an unlayered !important block. Asserted in e2e/reduced-motion.e2e.ts.

narrative.overview:
SyncTicket is a reading surface for a live system. The palette is achromatic by construction — every neutral in both themes is oklch(L 0 0), zero chroma, no exceptions — so that the handful of coloured signals in the interface are the only coloured things in it. A blue dot means Todo. An amber ring means In Progress. A triangle in orange means Urgent. Nothing else in the product is allowed to compete with those readings, and that is what makes them legible at a glance across a list of four thousand rows.

The character is refined and restrained: precision in place of expression. Hairline borders rather than shadows, a four-step type scale that tops out at 18px, one weight doing almost all the work, and focus rings whose contrast was measured rather than assumed. Density is operator density — 32px default buttons, 28px and 24px variants, 10px of padding inside a board card — because the person reading this surface is scanning a system's state, not browsing a page.

What makes the restraint credible is that it is checked. The focus ring was darkened from shadcn's stock oklch(0.708) to oklch(0.45) because the stock value measured 2.59:1 against the background and missed WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 on every surface the app has; at 0.45 it measures 7.44:1. Status colours are per-theme (a light step with a dark: -500 override) rather than one shared step, because the stock -500 family reaches only 2.15–2.89:1 on white and the badges render icon-only, which makes the icon the information. meta.test.ts recomputes every one of those ratios from the installed Tailwind source on each run, so none of these numbers is a claim — they are assertions that fail the suite when broken.
keyCharacteristics: Achromatic by default; hue reserved entirely for state
Flat in flow, elevated only when genuinely floating
Four-step type scale, no display tier, font-medium as the working weight
Focus as a first-class visual element, with measured contrast
Motion that is brief (100–200ms) and fully removable — the one long beat is news from a peer, and it moves nothing but opacity

rules.name: The Colour Means State Rule
rules.body: Hue is reserved for issue status, urgent priority, destructive intent, and peer identity. There is no decorative, brand, or emphasis colour anywhere in the product, and adding one is a defect rather than a liberty: the status signals are readable at a glance because nothing else is coloured.

rules.name: The Per-Theme Step Rule
rules.body: A semantic colour is never one value with a theme-independent meaning. Every status and priority hue is a light step plus a brighter dark: override, because the badges render icon-only and the icon must clear 3:1 on the surface it actually sits on. Collapsing a pair back to a single shared step fails meta.test.ts.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: font-medium (500) carries the interface; font-semibold (600) appears only on the few titles, and font-bold appears nowhere at all. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and colour in that order — never from a heavier face.

rules.name: The Four-Step Rule
rules.body: 12 / 14 / 16 / 18px is the entire scale. A new size is a decision about the whole system, not about one component; an instrument panel with six type sizes stops reading as one instrument.

rules.name: The Depth Means Floating Rule
rules.body: If a surface is in the document flow, it has no shadow. A shadow on a card, row, panel or column is a defect, not a style choice — border and tonal fill are how this system separates things. The board card's resting shadow-xs, long recorded as drift, is removed, and issues/depth.test.ts reads the card's and the row's class strings so it cannot return.

rules.name: The Circle Belongs to Status Rule
rules.body: The circle family is spoken for. The app ships six circle glyphs — circle, circle-dashed, circle-dot, circle-dot-dashed, circle-check, circle-x — and five of them are the issue statuses, which render icon-only so that the icon is the information. A ring, or a ring with a centre dot, is therefore not a free shape in this product: it already reads as In Progress. Identity and chrome draw from the system's other form language, the soft rectangle of its cards and panels.

rules.name: The 16px Adjacency Check
rules.body: At 16px on a 1x display the mark narrows toward the rectangle-family chrome glyphs it now shares a family with — panel-left, square-kanban. Any new rectangular icon is rendered beside the mark at 16px before it ships, and changed if the two are not instantly separable.

dos: Do reserve hue for state. Status, urgent priority, destructive intent and peer identity are the complete list.
Do separate in-flow surfaces with a 1px Hairline border and the Shelf fill, not a shadow.
Do give every semantic colour a per-theme pair (light step + dark: override) and let meta.test.ts recompute its contrast rather than quoting a number.
Do keep type within 12 / 14 / 16 / 18px, and build hierarchy from weight and colour first.
Do make focus visible with the 2px Focus Grey ring and a border change, identically on every control.

Do keep transitions at 100–200ms, and give any motion driven through element.animate() its own reduced-motion opt-out — WAAPI timings ignore the CSS block entirely. The exceptions are news rather than feedback and move only opacity: the 500ms quick-add flash and the 1200ms remote-change trace, which under reduced motion becomes a state, not a shorter fade.
Do put a peer's initials beside any peer hue drawn on a row or card. The hue says which person; the initials are what keep it from reading as a status.
Do let Kbd decide whether a hint shows on touch; opt in with showOnTouch only where the keys are the subject.
Do design the keyboard path first: every core flow is operable without a mouse, including moving cards between board columns.
Do draw identity and chrome in the soft-rectangle form language (the 4.5-in-24 corner, the card radius), and leave the circle family to status and to peer avatars.
Do render any new rectangle-family icon beside the product mark at 16px on a 1x display before shipping it, and change it if the two do not separate instantly.
Do let the mark inherit currentColor so one asset serves both themes; size it with the class (size-5 at 20px in the sidebar, size-4 at 16px in the header).
Do state limits plainly in UI copy when the system reaches one, and never claim durability, privacy or safety the system does not deliver.
donts: Don't introduce decorative gradients, glows or coloured washes. There are none in the product and they would undercut an instrument reading.
Don't add spot illustration, 3D renders or mascot imagery. Icons are functional Lucide glyphs that carry information.
Don't put a shadow on a card, row, column or panel. depth.test.ts holds the board card and the list row to it.
Don't use a solid Destructive fill. Destructive actions are text plus a 10% tint.
Don't add a second typeface, a monospace face, or font-bold.
Don't tint the neutrals. Every grey in both themes is zero-chroma oklch(L 0 0), and a warm or cool cast would make the semantic hues read as part of a palette.
Don't interpolate a network-supplied colour string into a style attribute. Peers supply a validated hue number; anything else is a CSS injection.
Don't give the product an identity glyph from the circle family, or any other shape the status set already owns. A mark that collides with a status reading costs the status, not the mark.
Don't colour the mark, gradient it, or give it a brand hue. It is foreground grey in both themes, and a branded exception would be the first decorative colour in the product.
Don't fork the mark's geometry between the component and the favicon. Only the stroke weight may differ (2 in-app, 2.6 in the tab), and only because 2px does not survive 16px of browser chrome.
Don't soften the focus ring to a translucent blend. At this token a /50 ring measures 2.32:1 against the background versus 7.44:1 solid, so the blend cannot clear 3:1.
